evidence: Clear module-based separation in the package structure (rma/cli, rma/helpers, rma/reporters, rma/rule, rma/tests)
Packages represent cohesive functional domains (e.g., rule for Redis data type analysis, reporters for output formatting)
No network boundaries or inter-service communication; all modules interact via internal Python imports
Single executable entry point (main.py, rma_cli.py) orchestrating core functionality via RmaApplication
Dependencies between modules are explicit but local (e.g., rma.application imports from rma.redis, rma.scanner, etc.)
No ports/adapters pattern (e.g., no clear separation between domain and infrastructure interfaces like interfaces for Redis dependency injection)
Layered aspects are present but not strict (e.g., rma.rule modules contain both logic and I/O; scanner uses redis directly)
Low average fan-out (2.38) suggests cohesive internal modules rather than distributed coordination
risks: Mixing of concerns in rule modules (analysis logic + Redis I/O + formatting) may hinder maintainability
Tight coupling to Redis and specific Redis client library (redis-py) limits testability and extensibility
Application layer (application.py) has many responsibilities, potentially violating single responsibility principle
